goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — New embeddable_hosts table adds no index on `host`, so every embed permission check is a sequential scan.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with columns `host` and `category_id` but defines no indexes. The embed permission path now calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which uses `record_for_host` and runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` on this table. With no (functional) index supporting `lower(host)` (and no index on `host` at all), this lookup will require scanning the table as it grows, so the finding is a verifiable performance issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?")` cannot use a plain b-tree index; needs a functional index on lower(host) (or normalized column).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` using `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, but the migration `create_embeddable_hosts` does not add *any* index on `host` (plain or functional). So the specific claim that a “plain b-tree index can’t be used” is not verifiable from the diff because no such index exists here. Also, lack of a functional index is a performance optimization concern, not a clear correctness/bug/security defect introduced by this change—especially given the expected small size of an allowed-hosts table.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — ensure_embeddable now issues an uncached DB query per embed request, replacing an in-process cached site setting on a hot anonymous path.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the check changed from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(request.referer)` (a pure in-process string parse of a cached SiteSetting value) to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, i.e., a database query. There is no caching layer shown in the diff, so this introduces a per-request DB lookup on the embed/comments path (often anonymous/hot).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:20 — host_allowed? has no caching layer at all, unlike the SiteSetting-backed check it replaces; a Discourse.cache/@@cache of the small host list would avoid per-request I/O.

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` does perform a database lookup (`where(...).first`) each time it’s called, so the “no caching” observation is factually true. However, the diff does not show any prior explicit caching layer in `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` either; it simply checked an in-memory setting string. The change to a DB-backed allowlist inherently requires a lookup unless an additional cache is implemented, and the lack of such a cache is a performance optimization suggestion rather than a clear bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:16 — invalid_host? adds a DB round-trip per retrieve call (including background/feed polling loops) where a cached setting was read before.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` from `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?(@embed_url)` to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(@embed_url)` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which parses the URL then performs an ActiveRecord query: `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. That is a DB round-trip each time `retrieve` checks the host, whereas the previous implementation operated on the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` string in Ruby (no query visible in that method). So the finding about adding a per-call DB hit is directly verifiable from the diff as a performance regression risk in polling/loop scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:18 — EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` materializes and serializes every host with no limit or pagination.

adjudication.rationale: The controller does indeed build the model with `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` (in `fetch_embedding`), so it will load and serialize all records. However, the diff shows an admin “settings” style screen intended to list/edit all allowed hosts at once, and there’s no indication in the diff of expected large volumes or a requirement for pagination/limits. This is a scalability/performance concern rather than a clear defect or correctness/security bug introduced by the change, so it’s not a strictly verifiable problem from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — record_for_host repeats the host lookup already performed by host_allowed? in the caller, doubling queries per import.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed.import` now performs a single lookup via `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` to obtain the category. The proposed finding claims this repeats a lookup “already performed by `host_allowed?` in the caller,” but no caller shown in the diff is demonstrated to invoke `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` and then call `TopicEmbed.import` in the same code path. While `host_allowed?` does wrap `record_for_host` (so duplication is possible in some flows), the diff does not provide verifiable evidence of double queries “per import.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:21 — host_allowed? instantiates a full AR record only to test presence; `exists?` avoids the row materialization.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host(host).present?`, and `record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which materializes an AR object. Switching to `exists?` would be a minor performance optimization, but the current code is correct and does not introduce a bug/security/correctness defect in the diff. This is an efficiency nit rather than a verifiable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — No index on category_id despite belongs_to :category, so category-scoped lookups/deletes scan the table.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts` with a `category_id` column and `null: false` but does not add an index. However, the diff does not show any category-scoped queries/deletes on `embeddable_hosts` that would verifiably require such an index for correctness, and the lack of an index is primarily a performance optimization concern rather than a clear defect introduced by this change. The finding’s impact claim (“category-scoped lookups/deletes”) is speculative based on code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Raw interpolation of the `embeddable_hosts` site-setting value into an INSERT string allows SQL injection via a stored setting containing a single quote.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the existing site setting value (val = embeddable_hosts[0]['value']), splits it into lines (records = val.split("\n")), and then executes SQL built via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is inserted directly inside single quotes with no escaping/parameterization, a stored setting containing a single quote will break the SQL (correctness issue) and can be used to inject additional SQL if an attacker can control that setting value before the migration runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` drops any pre-existing embeddable_hosts table and its data without warning.

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. That behavior is present in the diff and is potentially destructive (data loss) in cases where the table exists (e.g., a failed/partial previous run, manual creation, or re-running migrations in a nonstandard workflow).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Host format regex is anchored with `\Z`, which permits a trailing newline in a stored allowlist entry (`evil.com\n`), yielding an entry that can never match and bypassing intended normalization.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation uses `\A...\Z`. In Ruby, `\Z` matches before an optional trailing newline, so a value like `"evil.com\n"` can pass `validates_format_of` unchanged. The `before_validation` normalization only strips protocol and path, not whitespace/newlines, so the newline can be persisted. Later, `record_for_host` does an exact SQL equality match on `host` (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), so a stored `"evil.com\n"` will never match `"evil.com"`, effectively making that allowlist entry unusable. This is a real correctness defect introduced by the regex anchor choice and missing stripping.
